findings.issue: “5.11 proves a catalyst from the same step order” overstates the evidence. The consumed-then-regenerated pattern is valid for classifying a canceled species in the 5.7 mechanism exercises, but regeneration alone does not prove catalysis. Revise to “supports identifying a catalyst” or state that 5.11 connects catalyst regeneration with constant net concentration.
findings.evidence: As standard chemistry, and in CED 5.11, a catalyst increases the rate through an alternate pathway by increasing effective-collision frequency and/or lowering activation energy. CED 5.11 says a catalyst may be consumed in the rate-determining step and regenerated later; it does not make that step order alone proof of catalysis.
